Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test `isUnixSymlinkIsFalseIfMoreThanOneFlagIsSet` checks that a Zip entry with Unix permissions set to 177777 is not mistakenly recognized as a Unix symlink. The test expects `isUnixSymlink()` to return false when multiple mode flags are set.

The method `ZipArchiveEntry.isUnixSymlink()` returns true if and only if the Unix mode bits, masked by `UnixStat.LINK_FLAG` (octal 0120000), match this constant exactly. The code is:
```java
public boolean isUnixSymlink() {
    return (getUnixMode() & UnixStat.LINK_FLAG) == UnixStat.LINK_FLAG;
}
```
This means the method returns true even if other flags besides `LINK_FLAG` are set, as long as `LINK_FLAG` bits are present.

`getUnixMode()` extracts the Unix mode from the external attributes if the platform is UNIX, specifically taking bits from external attributes shifted right and masked.

From the bug report and test, a Zip entry has a permissions mode like 177777 (octal), which has multiple flags set including `LINK_FLAG`. According to current code, such a mode results in `isUnixSymlink()` returning true, which is incorrect because only having the exact symlink file type bits set should return true.

The core bug is that `isUnixSymlink()` merely checks the presence of the link flag bits, not that they are the only file type bits present, leading to false positives on entries with multiple flags.

This explains the test failure and the bug summary that `isUnixSymlink()` returns true erroneously for entries with a mode like 177777 having multiple flags.

The fix would require modifying `isUnixSymlink()` to verify that the entire file type portion of the permission bits matches the symlink flag exactly, not just having the link bits set in conjunction with others.

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
